the molecular analysis for the three genes was useful for screening for mutations in Japanese patients with C.M.T. disease, but causative mutation was not identified by the analysis in most of the patients with CMT.
we have developed a new molecular screening method for CMT patients, and that we found that the causative gene mutations in Japanese CMT patients are not limited to PMP22, Cx32, and MPZ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of Charcot‐Marine‐Tooth disease in Japanese patients.
the molecular analysis of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease in Japanese patients.
the analysis of the genetic basis of CMT in the Japanese population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the molecular genetic analysis in Japanese patients is not yet complete, but that it has already provided a significant number of new mutations and has contributed to the understanding of the genetic heterogeneity of CMT.

(1) the CMT1A gene duplication is a major cause of CMT1; (2) the PMP22 mutation is the second most common cause of CMT; (3) the MPZ mutation is the third most common cause of the disease; (4) Cx32 mutation is the fourth most common cause of this disease; (5) the EGR2 mutation is the fifth most common cause of disease.
